entries.reason: Authored: a place whose ground is a forest's floor stands in a forest. Trees stand beyond its rectangle about seven metres apart, the spacing of a grown wood a person can walk through, from three metres past the edge so no crown overhangs the place, thinning toward the place over the first 24 m so its edge reads as a clearing's ragged edge and not a wall of trunks along a straight line, and thinning again far out, where a tree is a few pixels and the row in front hides most of the row behind. Each is 5 to 9 m tall and a little over half as wide, the proportion of the packs' own tree. The count is a rendering budget and no fact of any world: at most 1,200, nearest first, which is 216,000 triangles of the packs' 180 triangle tree in one draw. Each figure is a chosen default, picked by eye; none is measured from a source.

entries.reason: Authored: open sand is not empty to the horizon; stones lie on it here and there. A low stone, 30 cm to 1.3 m high and a little over twice as wide (the first figures, 25 to 90 cm, were specks from any distance on a frame), lies beyond a sandy place's rectangle in fewer than half of squares 19 m across, out to 220 m, where one is a pixel high. No dune is drawn: a dune is a shape of the ground, and a mound standing on a flat plane reads as an object. The count is a rendering budget: at most 300, nearest first. Each figure is a chosen default, picked by eye; none is measured from a source.

entries.reason: Authored: open grass has a tree here and there, never a wood. The count is a rendering budget: at most 220, nearest first. Each figure is a chosen default, picked by eye; none is measured from a source.
